newsitem.title: FRANCE: Speculation surrounds Bis after founder's death.
newsitem.headline: Speculation surrounds Bis after founder's death.

text.p: Bis shares were suspended on Monday amid speculation over the outlook for the temporary workers' firm after the death of chairman and founder Laurent Negro.
Analysts said his death might increase prospects for Bis to take part in a consolidation in the industry marked by the recent merger of Ecco and Adia. They said Manpower might be a possible suitor.
"The founder's death will arouse speculation about the company and shareholder structure," one analyst said.
Negro, whose death was reported in the obituary pages on Monday, and his family held over 50 percent of the capital.

He told the last shareholders' meeting that the group was searching for an alliance but did not elaborate. Analysts said the search may now be accelerated, and potential bidders were certain to get more aggressive.
Shares in Bis, which touched a year high of 680 francs on June 4, closed on Friday at 533 francs.
One analyst estimated the share stood at a 45 percent discount to the level suggested by the Adia-Ecco merger terms.
